summary: The focused claim is established: the old harness passes undeclared jobj to object iteration, preventing compilation before and after the change.

assessment.necessity_reason: The build compiles this C++ entry, whose complete body declares obj but supplies jobj to an iteration macro that uses the supplied argument. This existing build failure blocks the target on both sides.

before.requirement: Compile object iteration with a declared object argument.
before.reason: The macro expands its object argument into json_object_get_object(obj), but the entry passes jobj while declaring obj.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The alternative supplied macro definition also uses the object argument.

after.requirement: Compile object iteration with a declared object argument.
after.reason: The same entry and macro argument use remain after the change.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The alternative supplied macro definition likewise uses the object argument.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The recipe compiles this fuzz entry as C++.

assessment.comparison_reason: The unchanged, undeclared jobj argument blocks the same object iteration operation before and after the selected object serialization changes.
